title: model and deploy an approved application resource design
input: The platform team defines the application components, allowed templates and deployment inputs.
action: App Design Center models supported application architecture and coordinates its configured deployment workflow. The deployment creates resources; their runtimes execute the actual application code and data operations.
output: The application owner tests the created resources and accepts the deployed endpoint and dependencies.
check: Compare the resulting resource graph, permissions and deployment rollback with the reviewed design.

title: assign ownership to an application's actual resources
input: The operations owner selects the service project scope and resources belonging to the application.
action: App Hub organizes supported application resources and their ownership or operational metadata. Registration supplies application context for operations; it does not deploy the application or alter data processing.
output: The incident responder identifies the correct owning team from the application's registered services and workloads.
check: Verify resource membership and owner accuracy against the deployed estate before relying on incident assignments.

title: orchestrate an approved order-to-ERP integration
input: The integration owner defines the trigger, field mappings and authorized target operations.
action: Application Integration executes the configured integration tasks and conditions, invoking supported connectors or endpoints. Each target performs its own business operation; mappings and retry design preserve order identity.
output: The integration records the accepted ERP order result and exposes failures for authorized retry.
check: Test schema changes, connector access, partial failure and duplicate triggers before enabling the production integration.

title: use approved dependency packages in a release build
input: The maintainer identifies supported dependency versions and the permitted package repository configuration.
action: Assured OSS supplies supported packages with associated security and provenance information through its configured access path. The build consumes selected packages; the team still validates compatibility and application security.
output: The pipeline creates a version-pinned artifact using the accepted dependency source.
check: Verify package origin, version pinning, vulnerability relevance and behavior under repository unavailability before release.

title: create a regulated workload boundary with the selected control package
input: The compliance owner selects supported control requirements, resource locations and operating roles.
action: Assured Workloads establishes supported workload controls under the selected package and configuration. Resource deployment must comply with those constraints; workload owners still implement application identity, data handling and required evidence.
output: The platform deploys the regulated application within the accepted boundary and assigns accountable owners.
check: Check actual resource location, effective restrictions and package-specific exceptions before claiming compliance coverage.

title: assemble supported compliance evidence for a bounded audit
input: The compliance owner selects the framework, resource scope and evidence collection requirements.
action: Google Cloud Audit Manager supports configured audit and compliance evidence workflows for its supported scope. Collected evidence informs assessment; reviewers determine whether the implemented controls satisfy the audit requirement.
output: The auditor reviews the generated evidence against actual resource configuration and records unresolved control gaps.
check: Verify framework applicability, evidence freshness, supported coverage and reviewer access before accepting the audit package.

title: query public blockchain activity for a research dataset
input: The analyst selects the supported blockchain dataset and a bounded address or block-range question.
action: Blockchain Analytics exposes supported blockchain data for analytical queries, including through configured BigQuery datasets. The query engine performs aggregation; public chain records still require correct interpretation and freshness checks.
output: The analyst reviews transaction or address aggregates and retains the queried dataset version.
check: Validate block coverage, reorganization handling where applicable and query costs before publishing research results.

title: operate a supported blockchain node for application access
input: The application owner selects the supported network and required node configuration.
action: Blockchain Node Engine supplies managed node infrastructure for the selected supported chain. The node serves eligible network queries or submissions; network consensus determines accepted chain state and transaction finality.
output: The application queries chain state or submits a signed transaction using its protected key workflow.
check: Test node synchronization, endpoint access, network support and confirmation handling before relying on ledger results.

title: build a runnable image from an approved application source tree
input: The maintainer supplies source code, supported runtime requirements and a pinned builder configuration.
action: Buildpacks detect supported application requirements and assemble the application and runtime layers into a container image. The build configuration determines included dependencies; the resulting image still needs security and acceptance checks.
output: The pipeline publishes the accepted image to Artifact Registry and deploys it through the reviewed release path.
check: Check dependency versions, image provenance, secret exclusion and application startup before promotion.

title: issue a private certificate for a workload's internal TLS endpoint
input: The service owner submits a CSR with the permitted internal identity and certificate profile.
action: CA Service signs permitted requests through the configured private CA pool and issuance policy. The workload retains its private key and installs the returned chain; clients must trust the accepted private hierarchy.
output: The internal client completes TLS with the workload using the issued certificate.
check: Test hostname validation, issuance permissions, renewal and revocation handling before enabling the endpoint.
